# USLP04 - Fix Shopping app console menus (input validation, cancel, demo data)

## Description

While manually testing USLP04 (List available stores) in the Shopping app (`app-one`), several defects were found in the console UI. This sub-issue fixes them and aligns the behaviour with the menus of `app-two`.

## Problems found

1. The in-memory database starts empty and `ShoppingDemoData` is never called, so the app always shows "No levels available." and the feature cannot be tested manually.
2. Choosing `0 - Cancel` in the level selection throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` (`levels.get(-1)`).
3. Choosing `0` in the main menu prints `Invalid option '-1'` instead of leaving the app.
4. Invalid options in the main menu are ignored silently, with no message and no limit of attempts.
5. Levels and stores are shown with the record `toString()` (`Level[levelId=1, levelNumber=-1.00]`, `Store[areaId=201, name=Adidas]`).
6. The store list shows a `0 - Cancel` option that does nothing.
7. `MainMenuUI` and `StoreListingUI` each created their own `Scanner(System.in)`, which can split the console input between two readers.

## Changes

- `Main`: load the demo data on start-up when the database has no levels.
- `MainMenuUI`: single shared `Scanner`; `0 - Exit` prints "Goodbye!"; invalid option shows an error with the attempts left; after 3 invalid attempts the app exits.
- `StoreListingUI`: receives the shared `Scanner`; `0 - Cancel` returns to the main menu; invalid option shows an error with the attempts left; after 3 invalid attempts it returns to the main menu; levels are shown as `Level -1`, `Level 0.5` and stores by name only; removed the `Cancel` option from the store list.
- `StoreListingUITest`: new tests for cancel (0) and for 3 invalid attempts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The app starts with demo levels and stores available.
- [ ] `0` in the level selection returns to the main menu without errors.
- [ ] `0` in the main menu prints "Goodbye!" and exits.
- [ ] An invalid option shows "Invalid option '...'" with the remaining attempts.
- [ ] After 3 invalid attempts the level selection returns to the main menu and the main menu exits.
- [ ] Levels and stores are shown in a readable format.
- [ ] All existing and new tests pass (`mvn clean verify`).

## Objective

Green phase of TDD: implement `OrderPartitioningService` (and the necessary domain methods) until all 21 tests pass.

## What to implement

`OrderPartitioningService`:

- `partitionAndAssign(order)` – validates the order and the fleet data; if the order fits in a single eligible robot, assigns it directly with no sub-orders (same behaviour as USEI04); otherwise:
  - partitions the items into sub-orders: refrigerated and non-refrigerated items are never mixed, and each sub-order respects the weight and volume limits of the robots; every item ends up in exactly one sub-order (totals equal the original order)
  - builds the list of eligible robots: READY, battery ≥ `MIN_BATTERY`, sorted with a `Comparator` (highest battery first, tie-break = lowest id)
  - matches each sub-order to a distinct eligible robot, finding a complete matching even when it needs a non-greedy choice (TC-23)
  - only if every sub-order has a robot: `robot.setState(IN_USE)`, `station.removeRobot(robot)`, `subOrder.assignTo(robot)` (status ASSIGNED) for each one, and `order` status becomes `PARTITIONED`
  - returns a `PartitionResult` (original order, sub-orders with items, weight and volume, and the robot of each one)

## Decisions fixed by the documentation

- State: `IN_USE` (not `BUSY`)
- `MIN_BATTERY = 20` (reuse the constant from USEI04)
- Tie-break: lowest robot id (deterministic)
- `PriorityQueue` is forbidden – use `List` + `Comparator`
- One robot per sub-order, never repeated
- All-or-nothing: if the partition or the matching fails (not enough robots, item bigger than every robot, no refrigerated robot, empty fleet), no robot, station or order is changed and no sub-order stays linked
- Invalid data (null or empty order, negative values, battery outside 0–100): throw `IllegalArgumentException`

## Definition of done

All 21 tests pass (Green confirmed). Zero failing tests.

## Objective

Green phase of TDD: implement `OrderQueueService` and `DeadlineComparator` until all 20 tests pass.

## What to implement

- `DeadlineComparator` – sorts by `requestedDeliveryTime` ascending; tie-break by order id
- `buildQueue(orders)` – validates every order first (not null, with id and `requestedDeliveryTime`, the two sort keys), then keeps only `PENDING` orders in a new `TreeSet<Order>` with `DeadlineComparator`
- `getPendingOrders()` – returns the orders in deadline order (a copy, so removing while iterating is safe)
- `filterByTimeWindow(start, end)` – `NavigableSet.subSet()` with inclusive bounds
- `filterByCustomerId(customerId)` – linear scan, deadline order kept
- `removeOrder(order)` – `TreeSet.remove()`, returns `true` / `false`

## Decisions fixed by the documentation

- `PriorityQueue` is forbidden – use `TreeSet` + `Comparator`
- Only `PENDING` orders enter the queue
- Time window is inclusive `[start, end]`
- Invalid input (null bounds, `start` after `end`, null customer id): throw `IllegalArgumentException`
- Invalid orders on load (null collection, null order, order without id or without `requestedDeliveryTime`): throw `IllegalArgumentException` and keep the current queue unchanged

## What to implement

`RobotAssignmentService`:

* `isFeasible(order)` – delegates to `findBestRobot(order).isPresent()`, with no side effects
* `assignBestRobot(order)` – validates the order; iterates through the fleet using a `Comparator` (no `PriorityQueue`); filters by: `READY`, weight ≤ maxWeight, volume ≤ maxVolume, refrigeration, battery ≥ `MIN_BATTERY` (= 20); picks the highest battery, tie-break = lowest id; if a robot is found: `robot.setState(IN_USE)`, `station.removeRobot(robot)`, `order.assignTo(robot)` (status `PENDING → ASSIGNED`); returns `Optional<Robot>`

## Decisions fixed by the documentation

* State: `IN_USE` (not `BUSY`)
* `MIN_BATTERY = 20` (configurable constant)
* Tie-break: lowest robot id (deterministic)
* `PriorityQueue` is forbidden – use `List` + `Comparator`
* Invalid data (null, negative values, battery outside 0–100): throw `IllegalArgumentException`

## Definition of done

All 17 tests pass (Green confirmed). Zero failing tests.

fulfilled by an available robot and assign the most suitable robot based on
weight, volume constraints, and highest battery level.

– Updated status of the selected robot (e.g., state changed from
READY to BUSY) and updated station availability.
